text:
The Blues have points in six straight (5-0-1) after Friday's 5-3 comeback over Dallas, sit at 14-9-3 with 31 points, and the goaltending has a new order: Joel Hofer took the starting job from Jordan Binnington this week, per ESPN, after Binnington went .844 over his last five starts. Hofer made 25 saves Friday, and the switch is the decision that will define the next month.

The streak is fun; the chances are less convinced. St. Louis has only 47% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) during the run and 48.5% on the season, and its points total runs about four and a half ahead of what those chances earned. Our playoff number is a coin flip, 46%. A lot of the scoring is coming from players running hot: Robert Thomas has 17 points in ten games on 9.6 expected, Jake Neighbours 12 on 6.5 after tying the franchise record with five assists in a game, Logan Mailloux nine in nine.

Thomas and Dylan Holloway are the core of the top line, usually with Jimmy Snuggerud, the team's top goal scorer, who has been out with an upper-body injury. Cam Fowler and Brandon Carlo have the best share of chances among the pairs (54%) but have been outscored 12-7. Watch Snuggerud's return and how long Hofer keeps the net.
